hook: Vinod Khosla co-founded Sun Microsystems in 1982 and was its founding chief executive before spending most of his career in venture capital. He founded Khosla Ventures in 2004, and in 2019 the firm became the first venture investor in OpenAI with a $50 million commitment. In September 2026 the Khosla family completed its purchase of the Seattle Seahawks, and he holds the title of chair.

quick_facts: Born in Pune, India, in 1955, he earned an electrical engineering degree at IIT Delhi, a master's in biomedical engineering at Carnegie Mellon University and an MBA at Stanford Graduate School of Business.
He was a co-founder of Daisy Systems and then co-founded Sun Microsystems, where he served as the first chief executive from 1982 to 1984.
He joined Kleiner Perkins as a general partner in 1986 and left in 2004 to start Khosla Ventures.
Khosla Ventures invests in software, AI, robotics, health and energy, and its holdings have included Block, Stripe, DoorDash, Instacart and QuantumScape.
He was ranked first on the 2026 Forbes Midas List of venture investors and was named to the TIME100 AI list in 2024.
The sale of the Seattle Seahawks to the Khosla family closed on September 3, 2026, with Khosla taking the title of chair.

achievements.title: Founding CEO, Sun Microsystems
achievements.impact: Co-founded the company in 1982 and led it as its first chief executive. Khosla Ventures credits him with pioneering open systems and commercial RISC processors there.

achievements.title: Founder, Khosla Ventures
achievements.impact: Started the firm in 2004 to back early technology companies in software, AI, robotics, health and energy.

achievements.title: First venture investor in OpenAI
achievements.impact: Khosla Ventures put $50 million into OpenAI in 2019, a stake Fortune reported at about 5 percent.

achievements.title: Incubation of Juniper Networks
achievements.impact: Helped incubate the networking company with its founder, Pradeep Sindhu, in 1995 and 1996.
